q: How do I correct calcination CO2 for kiln bypass dust?
title: Cement kilns: bypass dust correction
short: Dust removed from the kiln system, such as bypass or cement kiln dust, has been partly or fully calcined, so its CO2 was released too. Add it: tonnes of dust times its calcination degree times the CO2 factor. IPCC Tier 1 uses a 2% uplift on clinker CO2 when dust data is missing.
audience: Cement plants with chlorine bypass systems or dust leaving the kiln system

p: CO2 from dust = tonnes of dust leaving the system x degree of calcination x the carbonate CO2 factor of the raw meal. Add it to clinker based calcination CO2.

ul: Bypass systems on plants burning chlorine rich alternative fuels.
Dust sold or landfilled rather than returned to the kiln.
Not dust returned to the kiln feed, which stays inside the balance.

p: Dust tonnes from weighing, and calcination degree from regular loss on ignition tests.
